title: Envy
summary: When someone else's life stings — return to Jesus with honest heart-work, not comparison or bitterness.
graceGuardrail: Letting go of envy does not earn God's love. You are not behind His grace because someone else seems ahead.
framing: Envy compares and resents. It shrinks gratitude and poisons joy. This reset helps you tell the truth, receive mercy, and bless instead of bite.
why: Scripture names envy as a work of the flesh and invites contentment in Christ. Your story is not cancelled because someone else's looks brighter today.

steps.title: Grieve honestly
steps.explanation: The psalmist admits envy almost made him stumble. Honesty before God is safer than smiling while your heart sours.
steps.action: Say: “Lord, I feel sting when I see ___.” Do not pretend you are fine.

steps.title: Remember God's nearness
steps.explanation: Envy fades when you remember: God is with you. He is your portion — not their house, job, or timeline.
steps.action: Say: “You are with me. You are enough for today.”

steps.title: Ask for a renewed mind
steps.explanation: Rejoice with those who rejoice. Envy is conquered by Spirit-formed love, not by forcing fake happiness.
steps.action: Send one genuine blessing: a message of congratulations, thanks, or prayer for someone you compared yourself to.

steps.title: Choose gratitude
steps.explanation: Contentment learns to give thanks in your lane. Gratitude does not deny pain — it anchors you in what God has given.
steps.action: Write three gifts in your life today. Thank God for one aloud.

steps.title: Engage your calling
steps.explanation: Each person bears their own load. Compare yourself to faithfulness, not to someone else's highlight reel.
steps.action: Name one faithful next step in your own lane — not theirs.

whenToUse: Social media or news about others leaves you sour or small
A friend's promotion, relationship, or blessing stings more than it should
You resent people who seem to have an easier path
Comparison is stealing your gratitude and peace
sixtySecond: Admit the sting honestly before God.
Say: “You are with me; You are my portion.” (Psalm 73:23–26)
Bless one person you compared yourself to — message, prayer, or thanks.
Name one faithful step in your own lane.
prayer: Lord, You see the comparison in my heart. Free me from envy and teach me contentment in Christ. Help me rejoice with others and walk faithfully in my own calling. Amen.

scripture.insight: A heart at peace gives life; envy rots the bones.
Where envy lives, disorder follows — naming it is the start of freedom.
God is the strength of your heart and your portion forever.
